mcqs.question: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, which statement about corresponding angles is correct?

options.A: Corresponding angles are equal in measure.
options.C: Corresponding angles are always right angles.
options.D: Corresponding angles have no definite relationship.

mcqs.answer: Corresponding angles are equal in measure.
mcqs.explanation: If two lines are parallel, each pair of corresponding angles formed by a transversal are equal. Option B is false because supplementary angles sum to 180°, which is true for interior same‑side angles, not corresponding ones. Option C is only true when the transversal is perpendicular to the parallel lines, not in general. Option D contradicts the established theorem.

mcqs.learning_point: Determine whether lines are parallel from angle relationships
mcqs.question: If a pair of alternate interior angles formed by a transversal are equal, what can be concluded about the two intersected lines?

options.C: The lines intersect at a right angle.

mcqs.explanation: Equality of alternate interior angles is a necessary and sufficient condition for the two lines to be parallel. Hence option A is correct. Options B and C describe perpendicular relationships, which are unrelated to this angle condition. Option D is incorrect because the equality gives a definite conclusion.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a transversal in geometry?

options.A: A line that intersects two other lines at distinct points.
options.B: A line that is parallel to two given lines.
options.C: A line that is perpendicular to a given line.
options.D: A line that coincides with one of the given lines.

mcqs.answer: A line that intersects two other lines at distinct points.
mcqs.explanation: A transversal is specifically a line that cuts across two (or more) other lines, meeting each at a separate point. Options B, C, and D describe different relationships (parallelism, perpendicularity, coincidence) that are not the definition of a transversal.

mcqs.question: Lines l₁ and l₂ are parallel and are cut by transversal t. If angle 1 (formed by l₁ and t) measures 70°, what is the measure of angle 2, the corresponding angle on l₂?
mcqs.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when the two lines are parallel. Therefore angle 2 must also be 70°. The other options do not satisfy the corresponding‑angle property.

mcqs.question: Two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal. One of the alternate interior angles measures 110°. What is the measure of its alternate interior counterpart?
mcqs.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal when the lines are parallel. Hence the other alternate interior angle also measures 110°. The other values are unrelated to this property.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify interior angles on the same side of a transversal
mcqs.question: Lines p and q are parallel and are cut by a transversal r. One interior angle on the same side of the transversal measures 80°. What must be the measure of the adjacent interior angle on the same side for the lines to remain parallel?
mcqs.explanation: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary (their sum is 180°) when the lines are parallel. 180° − 80° = 100°, so the second angle must be 100°. The other options do not satisfy the supplementary condition.

mcqs.question: Statement: "If a pair of corresponding angles formed by a transversal are supplementary, then the two lines are parallel." Is this statement true or false?

options.D: Both true and false depending on the figure

mcqs.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal, not supplementary, when lines are parallel. Supplementary angles are characteristic of interior same‑side angles, not corresponding angles. Therefore the statement is false. Options C and D are incorrect because the relationship is definitively false.

mcqs.learning_point: Determine whether lines are parallel from angle relationships
mcqs.question: A transversal cuts two lines, forming interior angles on the same side that measure 85° and 95°. Can we conclude that the two lines are parallel?

options.A: Yes, because the two interior angles are supplementary.
options.B: No, because supplementary interior angles do not guarantee parallelism.
options.C: Only if the corresponding angles are also equal.

mcqs.answer: Yes, because the two interior angles are supplementary.
mcqs.explanation: When interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary (sum to 180°), the intersected lines are parallel. Here 85° + 95° = 180°, satisfying the condition, so the lines are parallel. Option B is incorrect because the supplementary condition is sufficient. Option C adds an unnecessary requirement, and option D ignores the given sufficient condition.
